problem: Prior surveys on world models are broad and generative-centric; they do not give a fine-grained, robot-policy-centric taxonomy that separates how predictive models are coupled with VLA policies, used as simulators, and used for video generation.
motivation: Purely reactive VLA policies struggle with long-horizon reasoning, credit assignment and compounding errors, and lack explicit predictive structure. World models, especially video-based ones, offer foresight, imagination-driven planning and data amplification, but the field lacks a clear organization of when and why they help real robot behavior.
key_idea: A policy-centric taxonomy of world models for robot learning, organized as world model for policy (IDM-style, single-backbone, MoE/MoT, unified VLA, latent-space), world model as simulator (RL, evaluation), and robotic video world models (imagination, action-controllable, structure-aware, foundation-scale).
insight: A probabilistic lens shows policy, passive world model, controllable world model and inverse dynamics model are different marginals or conditionals of one predictive-control distribution, which explains why they couple naturally. The survey's results tables show strong LIBERO performance across all paradigms (e.g., Cosmos Policy and LingBot-VA at 98.5 avg), so photorealistic video is not necessary for control, and long-horizon suites remain the differentiator. Whether video-pretrained backbones beat matched VLM backbones is left open, and the survey notes that Fast-WAM suggests the benefit comes mainly from training-time video co-training rather than inference-time imagination.
method: World model for policy: five paradigms (decoupled IDM-style, single-backbone joint video-action, MoE/MoT experts, unified VLA with future prediction, latent-space/JEPA-style) compared by whether future generation is active at inference and by coupling style.

World model as simulator: learned environments for RL post-training (World-Env, VLA-RFT, WMPO, WoVR co-evolution) and for evaluation (candidate ranking, MPC, policy/checkpoint ranking, reward/progress heads).
Robotic video world models: four capability regimes (imagination, action-controllable, structure-aware, foundation-scale) with a capability table.
Other domains: navigation (Pathdreamer, NWM, VISTAv2) and autonomous driving (GAIA-1, Drive-WM, OccWorld, DriveVLA-W0).

Benchmarks and datasets: three benchmark categories (open-loop, closed-loop utility, physical/executability diagnostics), dataset attribute tables, and aggregated results on LIBERO, RoboTwin, CALVIN and SIMPLER.
Challenges: causal conditioning gaps, efficiency, multimodal (tactile) perception, classical control integration, symbolic structure, evaluation metrics.
numbers_note: Survey paper with no own experiments; it aggregates manipulation results (LIBERO, RoboTwin, CALVIN, SIMPLER) from other methods, and none are on navigation benchmarks. Its navigation section is only a short discussion with no numbers.
results: The survey reports that competitive results appear across all paradigms; on LIBERO, Cosmos Policy and LingBot-VA reach 98.5 average and Say-Dream-ACT 98.1. Long-horizon suites and cross-benchmark generalization remain the main gaps.
limitations: Focus is mostly manipulation and video world models; navigation and driving get only brief coverage.
Result tables are heterogeneous and use inconsistent protocols across papers, so they are not strictly comparable.
Some claims remain open empirical questions, e.g., video-pretrained vs VLM backbones.
